audit.why: All seven rows read Wukong on both layers, which matches the packet chart and the 54.89% win rate over 1166 games. The two layers agree row for row, so no chart edit is needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike claimed Cyclone 'nullifies his R Purgatory totem' and that 'an airborne Locke cannot play around his R window'.
audit.why: Nothing in Riot's text supports a knockup cancelling Purgatory — it is a thrown artifact, not a channel. What the data DOES show is that Purgatory carries a grounding flag, so the real level 6 story is the reverse: once the zone is down your dashes are off. Selling the ult as something Cyclone erases invites the exact fight that kills you.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, whys[4] and the mid block rewritten around the grounding and the 120s rank-1 cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json via brief enemyKit (R flags: grounding, execute, slow, zone, projectile)

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. First, the ability name: the page calls his Q 'Ritual Nails' in eleven places, but Riot's own description reads 'Locke readies a set of Soul Nails to throw'. Second, the single most important interaction in the matchup — Purgatory grounds — appears nowhere on the page.
audit.why: Grounding shuts off dashes. Wukong's engage and his escape are both dashes, so a Purgatory dropped on top of you does not merely threaten an execute, it removes the exit you were counting on. That belongs in the cooldown block, not left unsaid.
audit.corrected: Soul Nails replaces Ritual Nails throughout; grounding stated in breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, spikes[1].text, whys[4], mid and wants.you[2]. Real cooldowns added: Soul Nails 10s at rank 1 falling to 6s, E a flat 10s (which the page's existing 'ten seconds' language already matched), Purgatory 120s at rank 1, W 18s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t says 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: His W is flagged as a heal and Riot's text says 'Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect'. A heal is a heal — Grievous Wounds cuts it. Telling the reader to skip anti-heal against an 18s self-refund is advice that loses the extended trade the rest of the page tells them to take.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now says anti-heal still bites and names the refund.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json via brief enemyKit (W flags: heal)

audit.why: The page's 'punish the ten seconds after each spent blink' is exactly right — E is a flat 10s at every rank. Confirmed rather than changed, and the number is now stated as a flat cooldown so it does not read as an estimate.

notes: Locke's Q is named Soul Nails in Riot's own description ('Locke readies a set of Soul Nails to throw'); the page said Ritual Nails in eleven places and I replaced it everywhere I could reach. His W, E and R names ('Soul Ignition', 'Ashen Pursuit', 'Purgatory') are NOT in the kit file — no ability-name field exists for this champion and packet.enemyAbilities is null — so I left those alone rather than invent or contradict them. Recorded as unverified. The packet's suspectName flag on 'Crushing Blow's' is a false positive: Crushing Blow is Wukong's real Q. Also unverified and left alone: the repeated claim that Locke fights 'at 125 range' — there is no attack-range field in the kit data. No Wukong cooldowns used — ownerKit was null in this brief. This matchup has no mirror audit yet (mirrorAlreadyAudited was false), so nothing was restated.
